outcome: Systolic dysfunction (mitral ring displacement, tricuspid S')
cohort: The cohort consisted of 34 HIV-exposed uninfected (HEU) infants and 53 non-HIV-exposed infants.
finding: At 6 months of age, HIV-exposed uninfected infants showed subclinical cardiac impairment (thicker myocardial walls, systolic and diastolic dysfunction), higher blood pressure, thicker carotid intima media thickness, and a higher prevalence of hypertension compared to non-HIV-exposed infants.
